headline: Sequence models predict cell-type and single-molecule regulatory activity from DNA
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Prediction
summary: Recent sequence-based models extend regulatory variant prediction to single-molecule chromatin, DNA methylation, and cell-type-specific expression.
synthesis: The dominant thread is prioritizing regulatory variants by pairing sequence-based prediction with functional genomic context. Within this set, that approach is extended across modalities. Wreath applies variant effect prediction to genome-wide DNA methylation, using a harmonized compendium of over 90 tissues and cell types. CellReg3D combines DNA language model embeddings with Hi-C 3D chromatin interactions to predict cell-type-specific gene regulation. CNN-CR learns compact shared promoter motif families that predict expression across 116 human biosamples, and these motifs are differentially interpreted across cell types. Mola, a model within the S2d sequence-to-distribution framework, shifts the target to single-molecule chromatin accessibility distributions predicted from DNA sequence. The sex-biased enhancer study quantifies eRNA from GTEx RNA-seq and finds that 47% of active enhancers show sex bias across 41 tissues, adding tissue-level regulatory context. What is new is the move toward single-molecule and cell-type-resolved prediction targets.
